concepts.gloss_en: Mishpat — judgment/justice (singular); the concept of judgment as the middle pillar, self-judgment, and divine justice that establishes the earth/fear

members.note: representative; used consistently across many Torahs as the singular concept of judgment/justice

concepts.gloss_en: Mishpatim — judgments/ordinances (plural); here glossed as an aspect of 'ruach' (spirit), a distinct contextual usage in lm1:10

members.note: plural form used only once, equated with the aspect of ruach (spirit) via Isaiah 28; grammatically and contextually distinct from the singular abstract concept. Under-merge beats over-merge — kept separate pending human decision on whether this is merely a pluralization or a distinct referent

notes: Singular משפט (abstract concept of judgment/justice, middle pillar) vs plural משפטים (used once as 'aspect of ruach'). Related but the single plural attestation carries a distinct gloss; kept separate per the under-merge rule. Human may choose to merge if plural is judged a mere inflection of the same concept.
